instruction: Configure my Ubuntu system to use Eye of GNOME (eog) as the default application for viewing images.

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting Eye of GNOME (eog) as the default image viewer in Ubuntu. Similar to the original VLC video player task, this uses xdg-mime to query the default application for image MIME types (image/jpeg, image/png, etc.). The evaluator checks if the default image viewer contains 'eog.desktop'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: Uses xdg-mime to query default applications for multiple image MIME types (jpeg, png, gif, etc.), which is the standard Linux method for determining default image viewers
Metric logic is correct: check_include_exclude properly verifies that 'eog.desktop' is included in the result string returned by the getter
Complete instruction coverage: The evaluator fully verifies whether Eye of GNOME has been configured as the default image viewer as requested
Expected value is semantically correct: 'eog.desktop' is the correct desktop file name for Eye of GNOME that xdg-mime returns
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts the most common default image viewer across MIME types -> Metric checks if result contains 'eog.desktop' -> Returns 1.0 if match, 0.0 otherwise
Edge cases handled: Returns 'unknown' if no default is set (correctly fails verification), uses Counter to handle cases where different MIME types have different defaults
No postconfig needed: Default application settings persist after user actions and can be queried via xdg-mime without requiring any UI to be open
